forces.title: Waste-to-energy integration boosts circular energy systems in EU.
forces.description: The European Union's new Heating and Cooling Strategy for 2026 aims to foster more integrated local heat planning. This includes the modernization of district heating, industrial waste heat recovery, and other renewable heat sources. Crucially, these local heat networks are evolving into circular energy systems by incorporating waste-to-energy solutions, biomass cogeneration, and residual industrial heat. This strategic shift leverages local waste streams and byproducts to generate dispatchable heat and power, thereby enhancing energy sovereignty and driving demand for waste-to-energy plants.
forces.source_title: Utilities at an inflection point: Four strategic evolutions ahead

forces.title: Retailer decarbonisation strategies boost recycling, food waste.
forces.description: Irish retailers are proactively developing robust decarbonisation strategies to align with government, investor, and consumer expectations. A core focus of their corporate social responsibility initiatives includes sustainable in-store activities such as improving recycling facilities, reducing food waste, and eliminating single-use plastics. With Irish households collectively disposing of an estimated €1.2 billion in salvageable food annually, the Environmental Protection Agency and leading retailers are collaborating on educational and portion control measures to mitigate this, positively impacting waste management efforts.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Retail Convenience H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook July 2026

forces.title: EU landfill reduction, policies boost waste-to-energy systems.
forces.description: A significant tailwind for waste management is the escalating reduction of landfilling, particularly pronounced across the European Union, which is increasingly positioning waste-to-energy systems as a preferred final disposal method. This trend is further bolstered by supportive policy frameworks, including export restrictions, feed-in tariffs, and carbon pricing mechanisms. These regulatory and economic incentives collectively encourage the widespread deployment of waste-to-energy technologies, aligning waste management with renewable energy generation goals and promoting sustainable practices.
forces.source_title: Sustaining the Private Capital Opportunity in Climate

forces.title: Public acceptance, logistics hinder waste-to-energy growth.
forces.description: Despite the growing relevance of waste-to-energy systems, their expansion faces notable headwinds. Public acceptance remains a critical challenge, often impacting project development and siting due to local concerns. Additionally, complexities surrounding feedstock logistics, such as ensuring a consistent and cost-effective supply of diverse waste materials, pose operational hurdles. Regional permitting processes, characterized by varying regulations and approval timelines, can also impede the efficient and timely deployment of these essential waste management technologies.
forces.source_title: Sustaining the Private Capital Opportunity in Climate

forces.title: Irish deposit return scheme drives consumer recycling engagement.
forces.description: The Irish deposit return scheme, "Re-Turn Ireland," launched on February 1st, 2024, has demonstrated significant success in increasing consumer participation in recycling. Despite initial mixed feedback, engagement has steadily improved, culminating in 900 million returns recorded by December 31st of the same year. This strong performance indicates the scheme's effectiveness as a powerful policy-driven tailwind, significantly boosting the collection and recycling of beverage containers and contributing positively to overall waste diversion efforts in Ireland.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sector Insights & Outlook February 2025

viewpoints.title: Ireland lags in recycling, indicating room for significant improvement.
viewpoints.description: Ireland demonstrates strong environmental sustainability in terms of low CO2 emissions and water stress, positioning it well globally. However, the country is noted to be lagging behind its peers in key areas such as recycling, energy use, and renewable electricity production. This suggests that while Ireland performs well in some environmental metrics, there is a clear opportunity and need for substantial improvements in its waste management and recycling infrastructure and practices to align with European benchmarks.
viewpoints.source_title: 2026 Ireland country risks: Strong tailwinds set to persist amid strong buffers
